completion_data.completion_summary: Completed Phases 1-4 of the 8-phase plan: per-task cumulative cycle budget with durable cross-invocation backing (Phase 1), a new orchestrate-churn.sh script for hard-mode three-strikes/burnout detection (Phase 2), wired hard-mode churn calls and base-mode drift/blocker aux signals into orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (Phase 3), and ported the H1 per-phase dispatch heading-scan/conformance-gate/marker-crosscheck/territory machinery into orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh with a new --phase-number flag on orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh (Phase 4). All four phases are independently committed with full test coverage (180+ new test assertions across 4 test suites); the full gate (run-all.sh, 69/69) and verify-deploy.sh (2 pre-existing, unrelated findings only) are green.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (and sibling batch-engine scripts) run under `set -euo pipefail`. Any `grep`-based command substitution that can legitimately find ZERO matches (e.g. "is there an open plan-phase heading left") must be guarded (`|| true`, `|| echo 0`) or the whole script aborts silently -- no stdout, no stderr, just exit 1 -- the moment that code path is hit. This is easy to miss when porting single-task SKILL.md prose bash (which is not run under `set -e`) into one of these scripts verbatim; add the guard at port time, not after a silent-failure debugging session.

This repo's shell test suites use two different collaborator-resolution patterns: some (test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-orchestrate-churn.sh) copy collaborator scripts directly FROM the agent-system source store into a synthetic fixture tree, so they always test source-store edits immediately. Others (test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, test-mint-dispatch-seq.sh) use a resolve_candidate() helper that checks the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/ tree FIRST and falls back to source-store only if absent -- so a fresh source-store edit is invisible to these suites until `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` is re-run. When a test for a script you just edited reports a stale/unrelated failure (e.g. "unrecognized argument" for a flag you just added), check which resolution pattern that suite uses before assuming a code bug.

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's own architectural mandate ("one computation of every admission verdict, never two independently-maintained renderings") extends cleanly to a NEW decision layer added later (H1's per-task phase-selection/blocked-reason/territory decision): compute it ONCE in the shared section before the --dry-run/live fork, store per-task results in associative arrays, then have BOTH the dry-run rendering loop and the live dispatch-building loop consume a shared filtered candidate list (e.g. probed_dispatch_post_h1) built from those same arrays -- rather than duplicating the decision logic in each loop or only running it in the live path.
